notes: Box score from the Heat's 123–113 home win over the Oklahoma City Thunder on Nov 22, 2026, from the Covers box score; all 123 Miami points and all 113 Oklahoma City points add up from the player lines, and the shooting totals (45 of 85, 15 of 38 from three, 18 of 21 FT for Miami; 42 of 92, 16 of 35, 13 of 19 for Oklahoma City), rebounds (48–38), assists (30–24), blocks (7–0), points in the paint (54–46) and Miami's biggest lead (20) are from Covers. The quarter scores (36–31–28–28 to 24–30–26–33) add up to both totals and match Daily Thunder and Bleacher Report; the 36–24 first quarter, the 67–54 halftime score and the 95–80 score after three are also in the Sun-Sentinel and Thunder Wire. The 20-point lead is also in the Sun-Sentinel and the AP, and the AP says Miami led wire to wire. Adebayo's line (24 points on 8 of 11, 8 of 9 FT, 15 rebounds, 12 assists, 2 steals, 2 blocks, 37 minutes) is from Covers, the Miami Herald, the Sun-Sentinel and RotoWire via CBS Sports (Yardbarker says 3 blocks, so blocks are left off his rings); RotoWire and Ball Exclusives via Yardbarker both say he had no turnovers. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Sunday's games.

It was Adebayo's ninth regular-season triple-double, tying LeBron James for second in Heat history behind Jimmy Butler's 13 (Sun-Sentinel; the AP also says ninth), with a career-high 12 assists and a season-high 15 rebounds; he completed it with a hit-ahead pass to Davion Mitchell for a transition layup with 8:09 left (Miami Herald; Sun-Sentinel). Pelle Larsson's 21 was his season high (Heat via Bleacher Report; Hot Hot Hoops). Seven Heat players scored in double figures (AP). The win streak is seven, Miami's longest since a 13-game run from Jan. 17 to Feb. 10, 2017 (AP). Miami played without Giannis Antetokounmpo (groin), and Bobby Portis Jr. made his first Heat start (Sun-Sentinel). Oklahoma City played without Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (neck strain, lower back contusion) and had nine players available (AP; The Oklahoman). Bennett Stirtz's 21 was a career high (The Oklahoman). Next: the Heat play at Philadelphia on Wednesday; the Thunder play at Indiana on Monday (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Bam Adebayo's dunk with 7:47 left in the third quarter that made it 74–63 (Ball Exclusives via Yardbarker: he drove to the rim and dunked; the Heat posted it as "BAM SLAM"). The board's Heat +9 to +11 is 72–63 to 74–63, which follows from the two-point dunk. The story doesn't name a passer or the angle of the drive, so it is drawn as the template's plain drive to a finish at the rim. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Miami Heat or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Adebayo's listed 6-foot-9 and 260 pounds (Basketball-Reference, Wikipedia), with arms at the default length because neither source gives a wingspan, in the Heat's home kit with No. 13 (Basketball-Reference, Wikipedia) and the default darker skin tone, since he has no approved look yet. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
